description: KatLang is a domain-specific programming language for calculations. This package provides the core parser, evaluator, and semantic model.
releaseNotes: Adds the reusable plain-text output-formatting subsystem (namespace KatLang.Formatting) so KatLangWeb, console applications, editors, and other consumers share identical formatting behavior. Three built-in formatters with stable persistable ids. `exact` is canonical display, byte-for-byte identical to RunResult.ToDisplayString — both route through one shared formatter-neutral renderer. `readable` is a structure-preserving pretty-printer: every sequence parenthesis and list bracket stays visible, and layout is chosen from BOTH preferred line width and structural complexity — a sequence with two or more structured children lays out multiline even when its flat text fits, a nested multi-pair string/value child renders one pair per line, simple flat values stay inline, and independently emitted root outputs are separated by configurable blank lines. `concise` hides only provably safe sequence punctuation, using line boundaries and indentation instead: safe one-pair child sequences become one line, safe nested multi-pair children become indented pair blocks (one pair per line), root pair sequences may stay flat, list brackets and the empty sequence `()` always stay visible, and no punctuation, labels, or casing is ever invented — structural line grouping only, never dictionary or record semantics. The string-delimiter policy (StringDelimiterMode Never/WhenNeeded/Always) controls quoting only and never alters string content: under Never, safe raw labels such as `neto` or `net_salary` still participate in concise elision, while ambiguous raw strings (empty, whitespace-bearing, comma-bearing, structural-looking, quote-bearing, numeric-looking, control-bearing, invisible Unicode format characters such as bidi controls or zero-width spaces, or unpaired surrogates) conservatively keep the containing sequence's canonical punctuation, and unquotable host strings always render raw. Natural structured results therefore need no spread operator for readable presentation; spread discards the parent structure and formatters never reconstruct it, while explicit empty-string output rows remain program-authored blank lines. New public API: abstract OutputFormatter (external consumers can derive custom formatters), immutable per-call OutputFormattingOptions (line width, indent size, newline, root-output spacing, string-delimiter policy, optional lower display limit), StringDelimiterMode, the immutable OutputFormatters registry (Exact/Readable/Concise/All/TryGet/GetOrDefault with ordinal lookup and Exact fallback), the bounded BoundedOutputWriter, and RunResult.Success.OutputRows — the read-only root-output row view that keeps separately emitted root outputs distinguishable from one sequence value. Every formatter honors the run's display-length limit with the existing all-or-nothing overflow contract, and all rendering is iterative and deep/wide-value safe. Formatting is host presentation only: no parser, evaluator, language-semantic, or Lean change, and EvaluateToString is unchanged. Display-compatibility audit result: canonical output was verified to contain NO underscore-specific handling — string content, including `_`, was and remains preserved byte-for-byte (the only underscore consumption in the code base is the numeric-literal digit separator in the lexer, e.g. `1_000`), a contract now pinned by dedicated tests across all formatters and delimiter modes.
